1. The Online Tuberculosis Information System (OTIS) uses different population sources for the calculation of incidence rates
for years 2000-2010 than those used in published TB Annual Reports. Hence, rates and population figures reported in OTIS are
different than those reported in TB publications. The most current population sources available at the time of release or
publication are used, thus the rates in both the annual reports and OTIS are based on the best available population estimates at
production time. OTIS 2023 uses the following US population sources: the Bridged-Race 1990-1999 Intercensal Population Estimates
(released July 26, 2004) for years 1993-1999, the revised Bridged-Race 2000-2009 Intercensal Population Estimates (released
October 26, 2012) for years 2000-2009, and the Bridged-Race Postcensal Vintage 2020 Population Estimates (released June 25,
2019) for years 2010-2020. Puerto Rico population estimates for years 1993-1920 are from the U.S. Census Bureau, International
Data Base; population estimates for years 2000-2009 are from the Puerto Rico Intercensal Estimates 2000-2010 (released October
2012); population estimates for years 2010-2019 are from the U.S. Census Annual Estimates of the Resident Population for the
United States, Regions, States, and Puerto Rico (April 1, 2010 to July 1, 2020) accessed September 24, 2021; and population
estimates for years 2020-2021 are from the Annual Estimates of the Resident Population for Selected Age Groups by Sex for Puerto
Rico Commonwealth: April 1, 2020 to July 1, 2021 (PRC-EST2021-AGESEX), released June 2022 by the US Census Bureau. Population
estimates for incidence rates are July 1st, 2022 postcensal estimates of the resident population of the United States for July
1, 2020, to July 1, 2022, by year, county, single year of age (range: 0 to 85+ years), bridged-race (American Indian or Alaska
